incidentbot: PagerDuty alert fired: inference-embed-queue-length HIGH (P1) — avg queue time 6.2s, 5xx spike on embed-worker, region: us-west-2. https://pd.example/INC12345

pagerbot: Auto-claiming page to on-call rotation: ken (oncall) — attempting soft-ack... :rotating_light:

ken (oncall): Ack'd. I'm on it, taking ownership. Starting initial triage.

morgan: Noted. Any obvious upstream (autoscaler/k8s) or is this model degradation?

devon: Seeing many pending tasks on embed-worker-0/1, OOM evictions in logs. Suspect KV cache thrash + pod restart loop. Pulling logs now.

liz (cs): FYI I opened a bridge to keep customer comms: ACME & PluginCo might be impacted. I can send an initial customer ping once we have ETA. :phone:

ken (oncall): @morgan @devon good. Please try quick mitigations: scale and restart cache-backed pods, avoid rolling restarts across all replicas. Keep me posted.

morgan: Agreed. Propose fallback routing to the smaller quantized model for burst traffic while infra stabilizes. That reduces latency and load. Thoughts?

olivia (sre-lead): +1 for fallback route. Also run a CV on throughput to confirm cost/latency tradeoff. If devon can scale now we can keep primary for critical customers.

devon: Scaling deployment and restarting problematic pods. Command:```bash
kubectl scale deploy/inference-embed --replicas=6 -n prod
kubectl rollout restart deploy/inference-kvcache -n prod --field-selector "spec.replicas=3"
```Applying sequential restarts to avoid full outage.

morgan: While that runs, doing a quick route patch to send non-SLA traffic to fallback:```json
{
  "route": "fallback-embed-small",
  "match": { "priority": "low" }
}
```Pushing canary now.

ken (oncall): Customer comms: liz, please say we saw transient queueing, mitigation in progress, will update in 15m.

liz (cs): On it. Short message sent to ACME + PluginCo: "We're investigating increased embed latency; mitigation underway. We'll follow up in 15 minutes or sooner."

devon: Scale completed, 6 replicas healthy. Restarted kvcache replicas one-by-one, no more OOMs in last 30s. Queue drain rate improving.

morgan: Canary routing active; ~40% of traffic for low-priority routed to fallback model, latency down for that cohort.

olivia (sre-lead): Nice. Can we keep fallback for 10-15m and monitor? If stable, slowly shift weight back. Also capture eval set for possible regressed outputs.

ken (oncall): Agree. I'll monitor alerts and prepare postmortem checklist. If anything spikes, I'll escalate.

liz (cs): Customers acknowledged the update, ACME replied they see reduced errors in their metrics — will confirm if UX improved.

morgan: Metrics look steady: queue length dropping from 120 -> 10, avg latency back to ~0.9s for primary + 0.4s for fallback. No further 5xx in last 2m.

ken (oncall): Great work. Marking this as mitigated. I'll keep watch for the next 30m then close the incident if stable. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

incidentbot: Alert status updated: INVESTIGATING -> MITIGATED by ken (oncall). Incident will remain open for postmortem notes and customer follow-up. https://pd.example/INC12345
